newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGB futures end Tokyo down before benchmark shift.
newsitem.headline: JGB futures end Tokyo down before benchmark shift.

text.p: Long-term yen bond futures closed easier on Monday, after the market's rise in the morning following falls in Tokyo stocks was checked at around 126.50 for the key March and 125.00 for the June.
Trade was technical ahead of a shift in benchmark status to the June contract widely expected on Tuesday, dealers said.
The market will consider the June the new benchmark when its turnover for an entire day exceeds that of the March.
The key March was down 0.09 at 126.30 with 39,800 contracts changing hands while the June was down 0.06 at 124.81 on 33,812 contracts.

"Given falls in stocks and the yen's firmness, short-covering pushed up the market in the morning. But its topside was later capped as no follow-through buying emerged from investors," said a dealer at bank's securities unit.
The key March contract ended Monday at the day's low. Its session high was at 126.55.
Traders said cash bond activity was slim as investors were mostly sidelined ahead of the fiscal year-end.
The yield of benchmark 182nd 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) was up 0.005 at 2.410 percent at 0653 GMT. The yield moved from 2.390 to 2.410 percent.
It is taking longer than usual for the June contract to become the benchmark because operators have not had to close March positions in the recent range-bound trade, traders said.

"If the market had moved in one direction earlier, those who lost should have closed their positions and caused a swift shift to the June, but the market has lacked a direction from mid-January," said a dealer at another bank's securities unit.

Dealers said operators who had built cross positions in the March, or those who had bought and sold the same amount of the contract, closed both positions at the opening, resulting in the March's turnover being larger than the June's.
But a shift should occur on Tuesday as the turnover of the June exceeded that of the March in the afternoon, they said.
The central bank's accommodative operation in the morning for a second successive day had a limited impact on JGBs because it was in line with market expectations.

Six-year JGBs to be auctioned on Tuesday may attract fairly good bids although the coupon rate is likely to be set at 1.6 percent, the same as the record low coupon for those issued in December, 1995, dealers said. Investors' demand for new issues is expected to stay high before the end of the fiscal year.
